title: Byte-Gated Register File
constraints: Four 32-bit registers. On a rising edge with `we`, byte b of register `waddr` is written only if `wbe[b]` is 1. Other bytes keep their value.

The register file is split into 16 byte-wide groups (register r, byte b), each with its own clock enable. `cg_en[4*r + b]` = 1 exactly when that group is written this cycle (combinational), so a write never clocks more than 4 of the 16 groups.
`rdata = reg[raddr]`, combinational. Synchronous reset clears all registers.
hints: Use the same enable to update the byte: `if (cg_en[4*r+b]) regs[r][8*b +: 8] <= wdata[8*b +: 8];`.
Partial writes are common (byte and halfword stores), so byte-level gating saves most of the clock power of a register file.

examples.title: partial write
examples.expected: only bytes 0 and 2 of r1 change
